meta.title: V3 - Final Design And Your Prediction

modules.intro: Last check before this becomes the hook that fights. Nothing after this.
modules.title: Still Legal
modules.aiNote: Unrestricted for driving SolidWorks. Measure in the model.

items: Saved as a new file. V2 still exists
Anchor hole still 1.000 in, throat still 1.000 in clear to the edge
Center to center still between 2.000 and 2.500 in
Projected full size mass still under 60.0 g

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: V2 preserved, V3 saved separately, all four dimensional rules hold and the projected mass is under the limit.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: V3 exists but one rule is broken or the mass was not checked.

rubric.criterion: V3 is a separate file that passes every rule including mass

modules.intro: Your scale article broke somewhere and at some load. Both of those are evidence.
modules.title: What You Changed, And What You Expect
modules.aiNote: Ask it how to build a shape. The change and the prediction are yours to defend at the rig.

blocks.content:
Upload a screenshot of V3 with the change marked. **Windows + Shift + S**, then **Ctrl + V** in an answer box.

Then predict. Your scale article was half size in every direction and it broke at a load you know. Your full size hook is not going to break at that same load. Work out what you think it will hold and say how you got there.

Being wrong costs you nothing here. Having no reasoning does.

blocks.prompt: What did you change from V2, and where? Say what in your scale test made you change that.
What load will your full size hook hold, and how did you get that number from your half scale result?
Where will it break this time? Name the place on the part, and say why it is not the place it broke last time.

blocks.content:
### Sources

- Hook Design and Manufacturing Guide, Dimensions, Design and CAD, and Where Hooks Break tabs.
- Your own scale test result, and your own simulation.
- Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, 10th edition, Budynas and Nisbett, McGraw-Hill, 2015. Load carried scales with cross-sectional area.
- IDEA AI Use Policy.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Screenshot is of V3 and the changed area is marked.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Screenshot uploaded but nothing marked, or it is V2.

rubric.criterion: Screenshot of V3 with the change marked

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names the change, its location, and the specific thing the scale test showed that caused it.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Names the change but the connection to the test result is vague or asserted.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Says what changed with no reference to the test.

rubric.criterion: Ties the V3 change to what the scale test showed

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Gives a number and reasons from how much cross section carries the pull at full size against half size, rather than from length alone.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Gives a number and a stated method, but scales by size directly rather than by the area carrying the load.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Gives a number with no reasoning behind it.

rubric.criterion: Predicts full size load from the half scale result with stated reasoning

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names where it will fail and says why that differs from where the scale article failed, or why it is the same place despite the change.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Names a location with no account of why it moved or did not.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Does not name a place on the part.

rubric.criterion: Predicts the failure location and distinguishes it from the last one
